rv.q: It's entertaining to watch the founding father try to navigate through the modern world.

The concept of Money Talks: The Musical is sound but it’s so devoid of wit, charm and successful humor that it’s interminable.
It’s a root-beer float on a hot summer day that sweetly satisfies.
It is a timely message Money Talks delivers with a light hand and endearing humor.
It’s a fabulous idea for a cheeky little musical comedy, and if the execution doesn’t always match the concept, let’s cut it some slack.
This is a pleasant way to spend an afternoon or evening, but don’t go into it expecting to have your socks knocked off!
Money Talks is an amusing, high-energy musical that struggles to escape comedic clichés and character stereotypes.
Money Talks’s biggest problem is its failure to communicate a convincing point of view.
Money Talks clunks along from one seriously unfunny scene to the next.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this whimsical musical about founding fathers as talking currency. While some praise Friedman's score and the show's playful concept, others find it superficial and clunky, with most agreeing it falls short of Broadway caliber.
